newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady to firm, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady to firm, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. shares were steady to slightly higher but trading volumes were light following Wall Street's record finish on Friday.

Dealers said the Dow's increasing volatilty continued to spook many European investors who were reluctant to take new positions ahead of Wall Street's 1430 GMT open. "Nobody is sure where this market is going," one senior dealer said.
"It appears that there is little to stop the Dow from going to the 7,000 level and beyond but if the bonds keep falling, stocks have to eventually come back."
The March T-bond was up 4/32 at 110-15/32 by 1105 GMT, while the March S&P 500 futures contract rose 1.55 to 768.15.

Amongst individual shares, General Motors was up $1/4 at $61-3/8 following comments from the company's chief executive officer that the automaker wanted to get "top dollar" for its Hughes defence subsidiary.
The shares also benefited from continuing speculation about a possible spinoff of GM's stake in Delphi, the world's largest automotive-parts supplier, dealers said.
Elsewhere, IBM, which reports Q4 earnings on Tuesday, January 21, was down $1/4 at $162-3/4.
